text:
anna: Heads-up — ephemeral keystore healthchecks started failing in staging after the egress-proxy bump. Keys still decrypt locally but the KMS proxy times out intermittently. Also seeing a drop in KMS decrypt audit events. Anyone already digging?

linda: Noticed it when the model-serving fleet started returning transient 504s. I can grab pod logs. Which cluster/namespace to target?

anna: staging cluster, namespace=redwood-keystore.

raj: I applied an RBAC tighten last night for keystore-proxy-sa (PR #6124) to reduce broad list/watch perms. Could be related if the proxy needs to read audit endpoints.

tom: We also applied the netpol egress rewrite earlier today (netpolicy v2). Might be conntrack/connlimit hitting the proxy. Quick check: conntrack count jumped when we rolled.

sec-bot: ALERT: KMS decrypt audit count decreased by 87% over last 10m for service=svc-keystore-staging. (rule: kms-audit-missing)

linda: Pulling logs now. Commands I'm running:
```
kubectl -n redwood-keystore get pods -o wide
kubectl -n redwood-keystore logs deploy/keystore-proxy --since=30m
kubectl -n redwood-keystore exec -it deploy/keystore-proxy -- curl -v http://127.0.0.1:8080/health
```

anna: Two short mitigations while we triage: 1) add an explicit egress allow to the KMS proxy IP/port in the netpol (temporary), 2) rotate ephemeral keystore material and failover to the fallback KMS endpoint. Prep for rotation in staging only first.

raj: Confirmed RBAC change only affected K8s API perms, not KMS calls. But the proxy reads the cluster audit config via a CRD; if that read fails it may suppress logging. Rolling back RBAC is quick if we need.

tom: I'm checking node conntrack and iptables counters. Quick snippet to check conntrack on nodes: 
```
sudo conntrack -S | grep expect
sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count
```

linda: Pulled logs. Proxy shows repeated: 
```
ERR dial tcp <kms-ip>:443: connect: connection timed out
WARN audit: missing decrypt record for request id=abcd-1234
```
Also see TLS handshake timeouts from the egress-proxy pod.

anna: That suggests network path instability -> egress-proxy or upstream KMS. Tom: does conntrack look saturated?

tom: Node #5 conntrack_count is at 96% of limit. We have a short spike correlated with the netpol rollout at 17:12UTC. Increasing conntrack table size is low-risk for staging.

raj: I'll open a P0 ticket and attach the PR/rollout logs. Plan: (1) temp open egress to KMS in netpol, (2) increase conntrack on staging nodes, (3) rotate ephemeral keys, (4) maintain audit scraping to confirm decrypt logs reappear.

linda: I'll run the netpol patch and collect logs after 1 min. Patch: 
```
# temp allow to kms
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-kms-egress-temp
  namespace: redwood-keystore
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: keystore-proxy
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: <kms-ip>/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

sec-bot: NOTE: created incident INC-2026-staging-keystore (severity=P1) and assigned to sec-oncall.

anna: After we confirm decrypt audit events return, do a controlled rotation of ephemeral keys and run end-to-end smoke tests. Also validate audit export pipeline shows the decrypt events in the SIEM.

raj: I'll kick off rotation now (staging only) and post the rotation job id here.

linda: Netpol patch applied, egress to KMS allowed. Waiting 60s to see logs.

tom: Increased conntrack limit on nodes in the staging ASG.

linda: Logs show TLS connect success now and decrypt audit events are back. Example: 
```
INFO decrypt success request id=abcd-1234 user=svc-model-serving
```

anna: Great. Next steps: (a) push conntrack/sysctl change to Terraform for staging, (b) revert the temporary netpol allow and instead tune the egress-proxy (connection pooling/keepalive), (c) schedule a follow-up to analyze why netpol rollout produced the spike (rate/ordering).

raj: Agreed. I'll revert RBAC rollback plan; not needed. I'll include notes in PR #6124 about the CRD read path being sensitive to transient network failures.

tom: Filing a short postmortem for the staging blast so infra can consider increasing conntrack headroom or improving kubelet conntrack tuning.

anna: Thanks all — keep the incident updates in INC-2026 and paste major notes here. :thumbsup:
